candidate.answerReason: The smallest slope above 1/2 producing an allowed lattice point is 50/99, attained at (99,52). The open interval may end there but cannot extend beyond it.

methods.label: Find the first slope that reaches a lattice point
methods.explanation:
The largest possible endpoint is the smallest slope greater than \(1/2\) for which an allowed lattice point appears. Suppose \((x,y)\) is such a point, and put \(p=y-2\). Then \(x,p\) are integers, \(1\le x\le100\), and
\[
m=\frac{p}{x}>\frac12.
\]
Because \(x>0\), this means \(p>x/2\). The smallest possible integer \(p\) depends on whether \(x\) is even or odd.

If \(x\) is even, then \(x/2\) is an integer, so \(p\ge x/2+1\). Thus
\[
m\ge\frac12+\frac1x\ge\frac12+\frac1{100}.
\]
If \(x\) is odd, then \(x\le99\), and the next integer above \(x/2\) is \((x+1)/2\). Therefore
\[
m\ge\frac12+\frac1{2x}
\ge\frac12+\frac1{198}=\frac{50}{99}.
\]
These cases cover every allowed \(x\). Since \(1/100>1/198\), every slope producing an allowed lattice point is at least \(50/99\).

This bound is attained: when \(m=50/99\) and \(x=99\),
\[
y=\frac{50}{99}\cdot99+2=52.
\]
Thus \(a=50/99\) works because the condition \(m<a\) excludes this endpoint. Any larger \(a\) includes the slope \(50/99\), which produces the lattice point \((99,52)\). The maximum is \(\boxed{\frac{50}{99}}\), choice B.
